maximum_inference: At most, this visual explains the chapter's design rationale at argument support; it adds no empirical, deployment, safety, transfer, state-of-the-art, AGI, or ASI result.

required_content.problem: The architecture needs a non-scale-only theory for how useful capability can increase without spending maximal cognition on every subtask. A scale-only allocation policy cannot, without additional state, select among routes using task-specific quality predicates, authority ceilings, total costs, residuals, or fallback readiness.
required_content.core_mechanism: On repeated workloads with multiple authorized routes, selecting the lowest-cost route that satisfies a fixed quality predicate and compiling reusable work can improve useful-task success per total contract cost over always-maximal and always-cheapest policies, provided authority, verification, residual, and fallback obligations remain intact. Select the lowest-cost authorized route in the declared candidate set that satisfies the fixed quality predicate; otherwise use the recorded fallback. Compile verified repeated work into versioned artifacts, tools, procedural memory, specialist routes, or regression tests, and charge their maintenance and revalidation costs.
required_content.worked_trace: A costed route ledger with quality predicates, residual accounting, and fallback criteria. Compile verified repeated work into versioned artifacts, tools, procedural memory, specialist routes, or regression tests, and charge their maintenance and revalidation costs. Use the seed/router/search/generator/verifier/residual loop to record candidate generation, selection, verification, reuse, and unresolved work under memory and governance contracts. Attach incomplete routing or compression obligations and their repair cost to the route as residuals.
required_content.failure_boundary: Cheap inference mistaken for intelligence. Critical context compressed away. Benchmark gains that increase hidden residual burden. Context construction, verification, repair, human review, regression maintenance, rollback, and residual costs remain attributed to the route that caused them.
required_content.evidence_state: This chapter remains Design rationale at argument support. Its contracts, examples, tests, or local artifacts establish only their encoded scope. A listed lower-cost authorized quality-preserving candidate causes the finite minimum-viable-route predicate to fail. A promoted result with open obligations and no residual record causes the finite residual-promotion predicate to fail.
required_content.non_claims: No chapter claim or evidence state is promoted by this visual. A named mechanism is not proof of correct implementation or useful deployment. A local check or formal model does not establish real-world enforcement. No safety, transfer, state-of-the-art, AGI, or ASI conclusion follows.
required_content.handoff: The next chapter is System Boundaries and Authority. It takes responsibility for To test whether cross-layer effects are authorized, the stack needs explicit identities for the principal, execution domain, operation, target, permission class, ceiling, grant lifecycle, delegation, and receipt.
